question: What is the primary reason for the heating effect in a conductor when an electric current passes through it?

options.text: The conductor absorbs heat from the surrounding environment.
The electric field in the conductor causes heat generation.
The movement of protons causes heat generation.
The movement of electrons causes heat generation.

solution:
The correct answer is __The movement of electrons causes heat generation**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The heating effect__ in a conductor is due to the movement of electrons, which collide with the atoms of the conductor.
 
• These collisions transfer energy to the atoms, causing them to vibrate more vigorously and produce heat.
 
• The resistance of the conductor determines how much heat is generated.
 
• This is explained by Joule's law of heating, which states that heat generated is proportional to the square of the current, resistance, and time.
 
• Applications of this phenomenon include electric heaters, irons, and fuses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**

 
 
• The heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to the square of the current (I²), resistance (R), and time (t).
 
• Formula: H = I²Rt
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Heat Generation:**
 
 
• Resistance of the material: Higher resistance results in more heat.
 
• Current passing through the conductor: Higher current leads to greater heat.
 
• Duration of current flow: Longer duration increases heat production.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• Electric stoves and heaters use this effect for heating purposes.
 
• Electric fuses use this effect to protect circuits from overloading.
